near_miss.why_not: Corpus searches confirm Irish formulaic repetition. Greek oath examples name gods but do not repeat the relative-clause specification of the swearing people, and the oath verbs are not the same inherited lexical pair. The Norse partners lack the formula.

The Irish birth prophecy, Norse Christmas birth report and Homeric shared birth-night lack a fixed cognate verb-plus-night phrase with a comparable special function. The Christian Norse birth report particularly cannot establish independent inheritance.

Norse ausa + vatn and Greek aphussō + hydōr are an attractive lexical pair, but Norse sprinkling a newborn and Greek drawing supplies for a voyage differ in argument structure and ritual context. Wider root searches returned further Norse birth rites and Homeric provisioning, not the needed independent common ritual formula.

search_lead.cognate: Greek hēlios ~ Vedic sūrya continue the inherited solar lexeme (*seh₂wel-/soh₂wl-); the seeing verbs are lexical renewal, not cognate.
search_lead.argument: The slab anchor’s immediate after-context is Iliad 24.558: cited words ζώειν, ὁρᾶν, φάος, ἠελίοιο. Priam associates remaining alive with seeing sunlight. Vedic wishing to see the sun for long expresses continued life. The joint life/solar-vision figure merits review beyond generic literal seeing; the precise Greek construction has light of the sun where Vedic has sun directly. This is a context-based search lead, not a two-anchor claim. RV 10.37.7d explicitly links living (jīvā́ḥ) with prolonged seeing of the sun.
